headline: Paper reports a learned contact simulator boosted real-robot bag-lift success to 19/20 trials
summary: Wang et al. present WorldContact, a contact-centric learned simulator for deformable-object manipulation trained on simulation trajectories. The paper reports state rollouts 10× faster than its source simulator on one NVIDIA H100, excluding rendering and disk I/O. For real-robot bag lifting, the same vision-language-action policy achieved 13/20 single-attempt successes (65%) after fine-tuning on 25 source trajectories, versus 19/20 (95%) after fine-tuning on an expanded 150-trajectory dataset generated with WorldContact. These are author-reported results from a single task and small trial count, not independent evidence of broad sim-to-real transfer.
